text:
Sam: Drafting a concise PRD checklist for the Optimize recommendations (batching, caching, quant). Wanted to share a minimal launch gate we can agree on. TL;DR: make it runnable in hosted, dedicated, and private with clear SLOs and rollback.
Maya: love this. Can you call out the acceptance criteria separately? that helps product <> eng signoff.
Sam: yea. thinking fields: functional requirements, non-functional SLOs, observability, downgrade/fallback behavior, customer docs, eval corpus + regression thresholds.
Jen: add edge-case tests: short prompt (<8 tokens), very long context (>=64k tokens if supported), repeating token storm, concurrent multimodel fallbacks.
Rafael: also constraint: quantization profile matrix per model family (int8/ggml/awq configs) and expected perf delta numbers.
Alex: don't forget platform: CPU cold-start, server OOM mitigation, KV cache eviction policies, and circuit-breaker thresholds.
Sam: exactly. Proposed acceptance criteria (first-cut):
- Mean p95 generation latency <= 250ms for 512-token streams on hosted small instance under 1 RPS baseline.
- P50 cost per 1k tokens <= target by model tier (we'll insert numbers in PRD).
- Regression on held-out eval set: quality drop <= 3% vs baseline for any quantized config.
- End-to-end telemetry visible in Console: per-route token breakdown, batching histogram, cache hit-rate over time.
- Canary rollout plan with automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions.
Maya: for the "quality drop <= 3%" can we be explicit on metric? e.g., ROUGE-L or embedding similarity threshold.
Sam: agree. I'll specify: embedding cosine >= 0.985 vs fp16 baseline on normalized eval prompts + top-1 generation BLEU/ROUGE thresholds per workload.
Jen: for canary triggers, suggest these thresholds:
- latency increase > 10% on p95 for 5m window -> rollback
- regression in eval score > 3% absolute -> rollback
- cache hit-rate drop causing cost >15% -> alert, don't auto-rollback
Rafael: scheduling note: quantization recommends to ship as optional profile selection in the Console (default = fp16, experiments = int8-awq). must include known failure modes (numeric instability, hallucination increases).
Alex: ops reqs: expose the following metrics via Prometheus: batching_queue_size, avg_batch_size, kv_cache_hits_total, kv_cache_evictions_total, model_quant_mode{fp16,int8,awq}.
Sam: good list. Also need customer-facing docs: how to tune batching.batch_size_hint, batching.max_latency_ms, and caching.ttl_seconds for common traffic patterns (chat vs. streaming vs. embeddings).
Maya: can we include quick sample configs? that helps SEs.
Sam: yep. sample in PRD (inline snippet):
```
# recommended for chat-heavy workloads
batching:
  max_latency_ms: 12
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  batch_size_hint: 16
caching:
  prefix_ttl_seconds: 120
  kv_cache_max_entries: 50000
quantization:
  profile: int8-awq
  fallback: fp16
```
Rafael: love it. For private deployments we need an extra note: KMS key rotation compatibility with cached keys and encrypted model artifacts.
Jen: acceptance tests we should automate in CI:
- small-scale smoke (sanity generation checks)
- perf harness simulated traffic (scale to target RPS)
- regression eval run against canonical prompt set
- chaos test: simulate one model pod down and ensure fallback routes correctly
Sam: also list of edge cases to call out in PRD text (we can paste into PRD body):
- prefix caching + streaming: when to flush KV to avoid stale tokens
- truncated contexts that split multi-turn instructions -> require intelligent prefix concatenation
- quantized model producing slightly different tokenization boundaries -> affects logprobs and reranking
Maya: do we have a plan for customer-driven asks? e.g., "reduce per-call tail latency for <50 token responses" — that's common.
Alex: we can handle via dedicated throughput lanes + higher priority routing. add to rollout plan: ability to pin a customer to a low-latency pool.
Sam: ok. Prioritization matrix in PRD will include: customer-request frequency, expected delta in unit cost, engineering effort, and reg risk. I'll draft a 3x3 quick matrix.
Rafael: Implementation notes: require runtime flags for continuous batching toggles, and a safe default (on). Also include a diagnostic endpoint: /_batch_state.
Jen: tests for numeric drift in quantized path: run 1k prompts, record token-level divergence points, sample review by ML reviewers.
Maya: who owns the canary eval corpus? we need a cross-functional owner.
Sam: propose: Eng-ML owns baseline creation + Product owns customer-specific prompt additions. I'll add an owner table.
Sam: action items before next sync:
- Sam: write PRD with above acceptance criteria + sample configs (due EOD Wed)
- Maya: prepare eval corpus + baseline runs (due Thu)
- Jen: prototype CI harness jobs for perf/regression (due Fri)
- Rafael: add quantization profiles and failure doc (due Fri)
- Alex: add Prometheus and alert specs (due Fri)
Maya: acked. I'll start running baseline embedding similarity tests tonight.
Jen: I'll spike on the chaos fallback scenario tomorrow morning.
Rafael: I'll draft the quant failure modes doc and share.
Alex: will draft alerts and add runbook notes.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline triggered: optimize-prd-checklist/spike-harness #42 -> started
Sam: thanks all. I'll post the PRD link here when it's ready. :thumbsup:
Maya: :eyes: looking forward to reviewing.
Jen: quick question: do we want a soft-launch with a single customer before GA?
Sam: yes — recommend a pilot with one engaged customer and internal beta apps. We can require pilot to meet 2/3 major SLOs for progression.
Maya: cool. I'll mark pilot candidates.
Rafael: one last: include a compatibility section for models with special kernels (e.g., FlashAttention variants). note perf expectations differ.
Sam: noted. I'll include a compatibility appendix and call out model-specific quant notes.
Alex: great thread. I'll drop an operational checklist into the PRD.
Sam: closing for now — will open PRD doc and ping channel when live.
